title: Common weather years widen uncertainty in rain-response loss at 170 south-east Australian catchments, 1951-2021
abstract: We test whether the reported loss of rain response in south-east Australia survives year differences and common-year uncertainty. We reuse annual CAMELS-AUS flow and AGCD and SILO rain for 170 catchments in 24 spatial cells. We compare 1951-1996 with 2010-2021. Separate-era models control previous rain and temperature. Year-difference rain slopes fell by 18.7 percent with AGCD and 15.4 percent with SILO. Spatial-only 95 percent intervals were -26.1 to -12.7 and -23.6 to -8.9 percent. Crossed cell and common-year intervals were -49.6 to +13.3 and -80.1 to +16.7 percent. The AGCD level slope retained a clear loss (-27.1 percent, interval -46.1 to -7.9); the SILO level interval included zero. One- and five-year blocks gave the same uncertainty in the difference models. Summed current- and previous-rain response gave no clear evidence for a compensating one-year delay. An exact regression decomposition showed that fixed previous-rain and temperature controls did not explain the main point losses. Thus point estimates support a lower response, but the short late record gives less evidence for a stable short-term response change than spatial intervals alone suggest. This does not remove the mean runoff deficit or identify its cause. Shared rain products, annual models, a short late era and approximate dependence models limit inference. Code, inputs with source credit, bootstrap draws, figures and independent numerical checks are included.
